subject: E-Commerce
title: The Power of .99
description: A quick, practical guide to The Power of .99.

hook.text: $9.99 feels much cheaper than $10.00. One penny difference, but the brain reads the left digit first.

buildup.text: Left-digit anchoring means your brain processes $9.99 as 'nine dollars' even though it's essentially ten.

discovery.text: Charm pricing (ending in 9) increases sales 8-25% compared to round numbers in repeated experiments.

twist.text: Luxury brands avoid .99. Prices like $200.00 signal quality. Charm pricing screams 'deal' or 'cheap.'

climax.text: Pricing is never just math. It's psychology. How a number looks changes what it feels worth.

punchline.text: One penny, 8-25% more sales. The left digit tricks your brain every time.

quiz.question: Why does $9.99 feel significantly cheaper than $10.00?
options: The brain anchors on the left digit and reads it as 'nine'
Stores round down in your favor
